Serbia also imports gas from Azerbaijan and has some domestic production, but not enough to offset the loss of Russian supplies.

Poland Voices ‘Reasonable Suspicion’ of Russian Role in Starlink Fire — Polish authorities said no arrests have been made in the suspected arson at a Starlink ground station this week, though some officials also suggested the case bears signs of Russian intelligence involvement, with Starlink access remaining a key asset for the Ukrainian military after it was rendered unavailable to Russian troops earlier this year.

Zelensky Asks Trump to Act on Lindsey Graham's Sanctions After Another Deadly Russian Attack — Volodymyr Zelensky has called on Donald Trump to act on the newly signed Russia sanctions bill, which would grant the US leader the power to impose a 100 percent tariff on countries buying Russian oil. Russia Hits Kyiv Pharmaceutical Plant for Second Time in a Week — Kyiv’s Darnytsia pharmaceutical plant was struck on Saturday morning, the company said, with the latest attack following another one on Wednesday. Russia’s 7th-Largest Refinery in Perm Reportedly Offline After Friday Attack — The Lukoil-Permnefteorgsintez refinery in Perm, over 1,500 kilometers (932 miles) from the Ukrainian border, is said to have been knocked offline – again – after Friday’s attack, with Reuters issuing a similar report after an attack in May. The facility is said to be Russia’s seventh-largest, with a reported annual refining capacity of over 13 million metric tons of crude.

Hungary Softens Position on Ukraine's C8 Platform — Hungary’s top diplomat has appeared more receptive to Ukraine’s C8 platform by saying on Thursday that Budapest does not rule out joining if it “serves Hungary’s interests,” days after PM Péter Magyar mocked the platform as “village football” as Kyiv-Budapest ties continue to fluctuate despite the ouster of former PM Orbán.

Overnight Russian Strike Hits School, Houses, Offices In and Around Kyiv — Authorities said at least five people were injured in Kyiv and two in the surrounding region after an overnight Russian attack that also damaged houses, warehouses and a school. Estonia’s New Narva Base on Russian Border Delayed Until 2028 — Estonia’s planned base at Narva on the Russian border is said to be delayed until 2028 due to local authorities’ holdups, with costs also rising by €5 million ($5.7 million) to €20 million ($22.8 million) as oil and construction prices rose in recent months. Ukrainian Drones Hit Russia’s Ilsky Oil Refinery Overnight — Ukrainian drones have struck the Ilsky oil refinery located in southern Russia’s Krasnodar Krai on Saturday morning, after locals reported a fire at the facility. Krasnodar’s governor said two businesses were struck without specifying which ones, with Ukraine’s General Staff later confirming the attack and calling it “an exercise of Ukraine’s inherent right to self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter.”

Switzerland to Vote on Neutrality as Russia Sanctions Hang in Balance — Switzerland is set to vote Sunday on a referendum proposing stricter neutrality policies that could bar the country from a military alliance with Europe and from imposing sanctions unless they’re approved by the UN. The referendum is pushed by a right-leaning group, with most parties reportedly opposing the notion.

Cyberattack Hits Spanish Train Operator User Data — Spain’s largest train operator reported a cyberattack that compromised some usernames and email addresses, but the company said there’s “no evidence” that financial information was leaked. Spanish outlet El Mundo said the attack shared traces of AI, with the incident taking place amid warnings of intensifying Russian hybrid threats, though no signs pointed towards Moscow’s involvement at the time of publication.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, September 25, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on September 25, 2026.

Why the Baltics Are Right to Worry About Putin’s Latest Reassurances — Vladimir Putin sought to reassure Europe while again invoking alleged abuses of Russian speakers in the Baltics – a familiar Kremlin narrative that has heightened regional concern.

Trump Administration Locks In Remaining $93M in Ukraine Military Aid Before Deadline — The Trump administration plans to commit nearly all $400 million in previously approved Ukraine military aid, with the final $93 million secured before the fiscal-year deadline.

Russian Drone Sparks Fire at Kyiv Office Building in Overnight Attack — Russian drone attacks continued in Kyiv after midnight, hitting an office building in Solomianskyi district following deadly strikes a day earlier.

Bipartisan Senators Urge Trump Not to Bring Putin to Miami — A bipartisan group of 14 US senators is pressing US President Donald Trump to rescind Vladimir Putin’s invitation to the December G20 summit in Miami and maintain pressure on Moscow.

Zelensky Visits Kyiv Maternity Hospital Struck by Russia as Fresh Attacks Kill 7, Including Israeli Teen — Russian strikes on Kyiv killed seven and wounded dozens as Zelensky visited a maternity hospital damaged in an earlier ballistic attack and renewed calls for stronger air defenses.

Kyiv Denies Bloomberg Report Trump Allegedly Asked Zelensky to Meet Putin in Moscow — Ukraine’s Presidential Office denied Bloomberg’s report that Donald Trump allegedly suggested a Zelensky-Putin meeting in Moscow during their New York talks.

ArcelorMittal Shuts Plant in Kryvyi Rih Due to Russian Strikes, Expects $1B Impairment Charge — One of Ukraine’s largest foreign manufacturers of steel products, ArcelorMittal, halted operations in Kryvyi Rih completely after four Russian missile strikes killed five people and injured 17 over the past five weeks. The company expects to record a non-cash impairment charge of about $1 billion.

Putin Accuses Kyiv of Striking Polling Stations: ‘We Were Ready to Resume Negotiations’ — Speaking to reporters on Friday, Russian President Vladimir Putin again pinned the blame for stalled diplomacy on Ukraine, saying Moscow was ready to resume negotiations after its Sept. 18-20 State Duma elections. He claimed Ukraine attacked the country’s polling stations, and added that the proposals for a peaceful settlement still exist – after the Kremlin decides “what is in its interests.” Putin’s remar
Russia Is Breaking in Ways Moscow Can’t Hide Anymore — Russia has entered a new phase, as the war increasingly reaches the system and population Moscow spent years trying to insulate from it.

Ukraine Speeding Up Production of Air Defenses Against Jet-Powered Shaheds – Zelensky — President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Friday that Ukraine is accelerating production of air defense systems after testing interceptors against Russia’s jet-powered Shahed drones. At a Stavka meeting, authorities also reviewed Russia's technological plans for 2027 and adopted measures to protect data centers critical to communications.

EU Agrees to Release €6.6B for Ukraine From EPF, Once Blocked by Orbán — EU member states agreed to release €6.6 billion (about $7,5 billion) from the European Peace Facility (EPF), EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on Friday. The fund, used partly to reimburse military aid to Ukraine, had been blocked since 2023 by Hungary under former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán.

McDonald’s Warehouse Hit as Kyiv Drone Attacks Kill 5 — Russian drones struck a warehouse used by McDonald’s and an office building in Kyiv on Friday, Sept. 25. Four people were killed at the office building, while the total death toll from Russian attacks across the capital during the day reached five. At least 27 residents were injured.

Russian Strikes Hit Ukraine’s Leading Textile Manufacturer and Other Civilian Businesses — On Sept. 24, Russian forces targeted multiple civilian businesses across Ukraine, destroying the production facilities of a leading textile manufacturer and a jewelry brand. The strikes also damaged a Titka Klara bakery and a Nova Poshta express sorting depot.

Witkoff, Kushner Meet Putin Envoy Dmitriev in New York — Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev in New York following their visits to Moscow and Kyiv earlier this month. Bloomberg had reported that Dmitriev was expected to receive new US proposals concerning the war.

WTO to Weigh Russia Complaint Over EU Carbon Border Levy — Russia initially filed a complaint against the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) in May 2025. The CBAM ensures foreign producers pay a carbon cost similar to what European companies already pay under the bloc’s internal emissions trading system, but Moscow argues it breaches global trade rules.

Russian State Media Deletes Opinion Piece Calling for Attack on Lithuania — Russia’s state news agency RIA Novosti deleted an opinion piece advocating military action against Lithuania. The column suggested using missiles rather than ground troops and followed Lithuanian moves to lift constitutional restrictions on nuclear weapons and foreign military bases.

‘Bodies on the Ground’: Death Toll in Kyiv Rises to 7, 59 Wounded — A Russian drone struck an office building in Kyiv’s Solomianskyi district, killing four people and injuring seven, including a child. Emergency crews extinguished a fire that engulfed cars in a parking lot beside the office center. In the evening, the number of casualties rose to seven dead and 59 injured as Russian strikes continued targeting the capital and an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) crash damaged another office building

Putin’s Reported Granddaughter Named Tikhonova, Despite Father’s Zelensky Surname — Investigative journalists say Vladimir Putin’s reported granddaughter is named Elsa Igorevna Tikhonova. Leaked Russian border records allegedly show that the child was given the assumed surname used by her mother, Katerina Tikhonova, rather than the surname of her father, ballet director Igor Zelensky.

‘I’m Waiting for Feedback’: Zelensky Says He Asked Trump to Press Xi on Putin — Zelensky said he was awaiting US feedback after asking Trump to enlist China’s help in pressuring Putin to end the war. He also outlined Ukraine’s preparations for winter, including efforts to secure more Patriot missiles and develop a European anti-ballistic defense system.

One in 10 Russian POWs in Ukraine Is a Foreign Citizen, Kyiv Says — One in 10 Russian POWs held by Ukraine is a citizen of another country, with prisoners from 55 countries identified, according to Kyiv. Kyiv says Russia has recruited nearly 29,000 foreign nationals since 2022, increasingly targeting people in Africa, Asia and Latin America.

Russian Drones, Missiles or Troops Could Test NATO Within Months, Danish Intelligence Says — Denmark’s military intelligence service expects Russia to intensify its hybrid campaign against NATO in the coming months and sees a low but growing risk of a limited military attack. Possible scenarios include drone or missile strikes, false-flag operations and a small incursion into a NATO border state, although a full-scale invasion remains highly unlikely.

Seoul Calls Out Zelensky for Admitting North Korean POWs Sent to South Korea — South Korean President Lee Jae-myung said on Thursday that the public revelation of the two captured North Korean soldiers transferred to South Korea was likely to cause numerous unspecified problems. Kyiv responded by saying the Ukrainian president had briefed Seoul on his intention to make the announcement.

Kyiv’s High Council of Justice Suffers Damage in Russian Strike — An overnight Russian attack damaged the building of Kyiv’s High Council of Justice, with at least six injured based on preliminary reports. The institution appoints, dismisses, and disciplines judges and prosecutors according to Ukraine’s constitution.

Trump Approved Patriot License Transfer to Ukraine, Zelensky Says — The Ukrainian president described a new commitment from Trump, but gave no date for the licenses to be issued or for production to begin. The US president initially announced the license transfer in July but later backtracked on the promises, saying Washington must exercise caution when sharing sensitive military technology. The missiles remain one of the few in Kyiv’s arsenal capable of downing Russian ballistic missiles.

‘Save Lives’: Stubb Urges Musk to Expand Starlink Access for Ukraine — Finnish President Alexander Stubb appealed to Elon Musk to allow Ukraine to use Starlink against Russian ballistic missile launchers inside Russia and occupied Ukrainian territory. Stubb said the expanded access could compensate partly for Ukraine’s shortage of Patriot interceptors and save civilian lives ahead of winter.

Ukraine’s Troops Helped Push Putin’s ‘Anchorage’ Demands Off Peace Talks Agenda, Zelensky Says — President Volodymyr Zelensky says negotiations have moved away from the so-called “Anchorage agreements,” crediting Ukraine’s armed forces and US negotiators. He warned that Putin’s ambitions extend beyond the Donbas.

US Proposes Ukraine-Russia Trilateral Talks in UAE, Zelensky Says — US proposes technical-level Ukraine-Russia talks in the UAE, Zelensky says, as Washington also invites Putin to the G20 summit in Miami. The Kremlin says it is too early to discuss Putin’s attendance.

14-Year-Old Boy Killed as Russian Drone Hits Kyiv High-Rise — A 14-year-old boy was killed and three people injured after a Russian drone struck a residential high-rise in Kyiv on Friday. The attack hit the Pechersk district as Russia launched nearly 300 drones at Ukraine overnight.

Russia is Planning ‘Something Big’ This Year, Sikorski Warns as Escalation Fears Grow — Poland’s Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski warned that Russia may be preparing a major operation this year, potentially including a false-flag attack to justify mobilization. He said Russia could test NATO through hybrid or limited actions, including in the Baltics or via Belarus, while continuing its war against Ukraine and targeting its energy infrastructure.

Ukrainian Drone Barrage Hits Russian Refineries, Missile-Parts Plant — Ukrainian drones struck two major Russian oil refineries and a defense plant overnight, causing fires, damage and injuries. The targets included the Lukoil-Permnefteorgsintez refinery, Russia’s Iskra defense plant, and the Novoshakhtinsk refinery in Rostov Region.

EU Membership for Ukraine Is Key to Europe’s Security — Despite concerns over corruption, agriculture, budgets and enlargement costs, Ukraine’s EU membership could become central to any future peace settlement. The argument: political will, transition periods and a firm accession date could anchor Ukraine’s reforms, investment and Europe’s long-term security.

A Trade Truce, Not Peace: What Trump and Xi Are Really Negotiating — The upcoming Trump-Xi summit is expected to center on extending the US-China trade truce set to expire on Nov. 10, with Beijing seeking a long-term extension and Washington favoring a shorter arrangement to maintain negotiating leverage.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, September 24, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on September 24, 2026.

Ukraine Has Obtained Detailed Russian Plans for Winter Strikes, Energy Minister Says — Ukraine has obtained detailed Russian plans for winter strikes on energy, heating and water infrastructure, while more than 200 protective structures have been built around priority targets.

Russia Launches New Ballistic Threat Toward Kyiv After Massive Overnight Attack — Russia triggered fresh alerts in Kyiv early Sept. 25, hours after a deadly combined missile and drone attack on the capital.

Can Trump and Xi Turn Leverage Into a Russia Deal – and What Are the Stakes for Ukraine? — Trump’s sanctions authority and Xi’s economic influence over Russia could reshape diplomacy around the war. For Ukraine, the key question is whether that leverage is actually used while Moscow keeps a backchannel open through Kirill Dmitriev’s US mission.

Macron Dismisses Claim CIA Warned France of Russian Drone Strike — France denied receiving a CIA warning about a possible Russian drone strike targeting southern Europe as regional security concerns remain high.

NATO Steps Up Intelligence-Sharing Over Russian Sabotage Threat — NATO is increasing intelligence-sharing among allies after a series of suspected Russian sabotage incidents, Supreme Allied Commander Europe General Alexus Grynkewich said. His remarks follow a Danish warning that Moscow could attempt a limited attack on NATO members.

EU Sanctions Former RT France Chief Xenia Fedorova — The EU added former RT France chief Xenia Fedorova to its sanctions list on Thursday for spreading pro-Kremlin narratives in French media. The move comes after France ordered her expulsion in July and as Russian disinformation targets France’s 2027 elections.

EU Vows to Condemn Russia at G20 Even if Putin Attends — The EU said it will condemn Russia’s war on Ukraine during December’s G20 summit in Miami regardless of whether Russian President Vladimir Putin accepts Washington’s invitation. EU foreign chief Kaja Kallas criticized the invitation, while French far-right leader Marine Le Pen welcomed it.
Russia Solved the Censorship Problem — When a channel’s audience is still there but YouTube suddenly stops sending new viewers, the real question is what changed inside the recommendation system.

Ukraine Opens Second EU Negotiating Cluster as Reform Delivery Shapes Further Accession Progress, KSE Institute Says — KSE Institute’s Ukraine EU Accession Tracker for Q3 2026 finds measurable progress in negotiations and legislation, but slower delivery on rule-of-law commitments. Two of six negotiating clusters and seven of 33 chapters are open, while only one of ten Kachka–Kos plan points has been fully completed.

Le Pen Rules Out Ukraine Funding as Russia Targets French Election — Marine Le Pen, the far-right National Rally leader and front-runner to succeed Emmanuel Macron in France’s 2027 presidential election, said she would end financial aid to Ukraine and denied France is at war with Russia, as European leaders warn Moscow plans to increase its hybrid strikes against NATO countries.

UK to Keep Sanctions on 2 Russian Oligarchs Despite EU Compromise — UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham privately told President Volodymyr Zelensky on Wednesday that he disagreed with the EU’s decision to delist Russian oligarchs Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman, according to Bloomberg. The move was a compromise that extended EU sanctions on about 3,000 individuals and entities for three years on Monday. The decision prompted Latvia and Estonia to act nationally.

Putin Envoy Heads to New York as Washington Renews Ukraine Diplomacy Effort — Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev is set to meet US officials in New York to discuss Washington’s latest proposals for de-escalating Russia’s war against Ukraine. The US plan reportedly includes a reciprocal halt to attacks on energy infrastructure, reopening the Black Sea grain corridor, and arranging trilateral talks.

Ukraine’s Draft 2027 State Budget Envisages UAH 1.67 Trillion Deficit, KSE Institute Says — KSE Institute’s analysis of Ukraine’s Draft State Budget 2027 projects revenues of UAH 5.65 trillion and a deficit of UAH 1.67 trillion, or 15% of GDP. Ministry of Defence spending is planned at UAH 3.76 trillion, while $32.6 billion of planned external loans currently has no confirmed financing sources or corresponding partner commitments.

EU Approves $3.4B Transfer to Ukraine, Based on Kyiv Reforms — The EU approved a $3.4 billion disbursement to Ukraine on Sept. 24 after Kyiv completed 10 targeted reform steps. The package includes $909 million in initial loan support, and integrates a $105.1 million non-repayable contribution from Norway.

Where the Harvest Has Nowhere to Go — Russian attacks have crippled Ukraine's Black Sea export routes, crashing local grain prices even as global wheat futures rise. In Kherson's Posad-Pokrovske, farmers Vyacheslav Dolholutskyi and Fedor Shpak work fields under drone threat, supplementing income through irrigation-canal jobs to survive a harvest they can barely sell. Both rebuilt after fleeing occupation in 2022. Now, with wheat prices halved and no compensation, they face a deeper question: whe

Zelensky Names 3 Steps Trump Is Pushing to Restart Ukraine-Russia Peace Talks — Zelensky said the US is pushing three steps: an energy ceasefire, reopening the Black Sea grain corridor and a trilateral US-Ukraine-Russia meeting. Kyiv is ready to discuss the proposals but remains skeptical of Putin’s willingness to engage.

Estonia Targets 2 Russian Oligarchs With National Sanctions — On Thursday, Estonia imposed national sanctions on Mikhail Fridman and Alisher Usmanov, two Russian oligarchs recently delisted from EU sanctions, citing their “support [for] Russia’s aggression against Ukraine.” The EU’s decision was also criticized by Ukraine’s sanctions envoy and president, the latter calling it “suicidal and counterproductive.”

NATO Scrambles F-16s and F-18s in Failed Intercept of Russian War Drone Over Romania — A Russian Geran drone entered Romanian airspace from Ukraine near Botoșani Thursday morning amid a major attack on Ukraine, flew ~4 minutes, and crashed near Solca without interception by scrambled F-16s. Parallel Moldova violations and a prior Polish Mi-8 incident highlight ongoing NATO struggles against low-cost Russian drones.

Zelensky Announces New Patriot Package in Tight-Lipped Remarks — Zelensky said Ukraine secured a new deal for Patriots on Wednesday but did not say from whom, how many, and when they might arrive. While Kyiv has warned of critical Patriot shortages, Zelensky also claimed Ukraine shot down 60% of incoming Russian ballistic missiles overnight on Thursday in a modest boost from the 29% intercept rate seen in July, suggesting some help has arrived.

Poland Evacuates Two Border Crossings as Russian Attacks Hit Western Ukraine — Poland temporarily evacuated two border crossings with Ukraine as Russia attacked near the Polish border, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said. The move came amid continued Russian drone strikes across western Ukraine and major rail delays.

Kremlin Says Invitation to Moscow Still Stands After Zelensky Told He’d Get There ‘On a Rocket’ — Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov claimed President Volodymyr Zelensky had not rejected Moscow’s invitation for talks, despite Zelensky telling a Russian reporter that he would travel there “on a f***ing rocket.” Kyiv has repeatedly rejected Moscow as a venue and proposed negotiations in a neutral country.

‘They Were Sorting Vegetables’: Russian Attack Kills 6 Workers in Kharkiv Oblast — A Russian attack on a vegetable storage facility in Kharkiv region killed 6 workers and wounded 12 on Sept. 24. The attack came during a massive overnight barrage that included three waves of ballistic missiles and drones that also hit Kyiv, killing 2 and wounding at least 6 more.

Kanye’s St. Petersburg Concerts Reportedly Scrapped — The planned October concerts in Russia of US rapper Kanye West, who sang “I beat up the p***y for Ukraine” in one of his musical compositions, reportedly fell through days after being removed from the official tour schedule, with the planning troubled by venues pulling out and Russian officials criticizing West’s antics soon after they were announced.
Zelensky Says He Would Visit Moscow ‘On a Rocket’ — Zelensky’s reply to Russian reporters in New York echoed a position he made explicit in January: he is willing to meet Putin, but not in Moscow.

‘Needed Every Day’: Zelensky, Rutte Talk Patriots — President Volodymyr Zelensky asked NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte to help secure a winter air defense package after Russia launched three waves of ballistic missiles at Kyiv. Zelensky said Ukraine is improving its defenses against cruise missiles and jet-powered drones, but still relies on Patriot interceptors to counter ballistic threats.

Fire at Polish Starlink Hub Sparks Sabotage Investigation — Poland’s Deputy Prime Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said a fire at the Wola Krobowska Starlink ground station in central Poland is being treated by authorities as a likely sabotage attempt. The blaze damaged the facility's power systems and temporarily disrupted internet connectivity provided through the station, which serves parts of Central and Eastern Europe and supports communications used by Ukraine.

Ukraine Sent North Korean POWs to South Korea, Zelensky Says — Zelensky said the two North Korean soldiers captured in 2024 departed for South Korea “recently” during his UN speech on Wednesday. The two initially rejected asylum offered by Seoul but reportedly changed their minds close to a year later, with reports in late 2025 suggesting they wanted to live in South Korea.

Russian Radars and Drone Launch Site Damaged by Ukraine — Ukrainian forces struck two Russian radar stations, a facility used to store and launch attack drones near Donetsk, and a fuel depot in the occupied Zaporizhzhia region, the General Staff said. The military did not specify the weapons used or the extent of the damage.

Russia’s Global Recruitment Pipeline: How Russia Hunts the World’s Poor to Feed Its War in Ukraine – Part 2 — The second part of this investigation examines the global reach of Russia’s foreign recruitment campaign, focusing on South Asia, Latin America, Indonesia, and former Soviet states. Ukrainian officials and human rights organizations describe a recurring pattern: promises of civilian employment, fast-tracked citizenship, or lucrative earnings that lead instead to military service and fron

CIA Warns of Potential Russian Drone Strikes From Shadow Fleet Vessels — According to a report by Spain's El Mundo, the CIA has warned European allies that Russia may be planning to launch drones from shadow fleet vessels in the Mediterranean Sea. The alleged attacks could target countries such as Spain, France, and Italy and form part of a broader pattern of hybrid operations against NATO members supporting Ukraine.

Kremlin Says Too Early to Discuss Putin’s G20 Trip After Welcoming US Invitation — The Kremlin welcomed a US invitation for Russian President Vladimir Putin to attend the G20 summit in Miami on Wednesday, only to walk back its statement on Thursday by saying it was too early to talk about it. The invitation came as Washington pushed for negotiations to end the war, continuing the diplomatic momentum achieved during the early September visit to Moscow and Kyiv by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared

Ukraine Pushes Forward in 4 Frontline Sectors as Russia Struggles for Gains — Ukrainian forces recently advanced in 4 frontline sectors, including near Kupyansk, Chasiv Yar and two areas of Dnipropetrovsk region, as per ISW. Russian forces also made limited gains near Kostyantynivka and Dobropillya, but failed to advance in northern Kharkiv region.

‘No Other Choice’: Zelensky Warns Russia of Winter Strikes — President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that Ukraine would make the coming winter “painful” for Russia if Moscow continues striking Ukrainian energy and heating infrastructure. Speaking at the UN General Assembly, he invoked “General Winter” – traditionally viewed as Russia’s ally – and said it could instead help those defending themselves from Russian aggression.

Russia’s Oil Sites Hit Again in Overnight Ukrainian Drone Attack — Russian officials reported damage to an oil depot in the Rostov region and a fire at an unidentified facility in the Krasnodar region. A Ukrainian monitoring channel said the second site was another oil depot.

Russian Envoy Dmitriev Heads to US for Talks With Witkoff, Kushner — Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev is heading to New York for talks with Trump administration officials as Ukraine pushes an unconditional ceasefire backed by 50 countries. Moscow has yet to respond, while US-Russia contacts continue over the war and potential peace talks

Russia Sanctions Lifted for Two Oligarchs — The article criticizes France and the EU over reported efforts to ease sanctions on Russian billionaires Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman as part of a diplomatic deal involving Azerbaijan and detained French citizens. Critics, including Yulia Navalnaya, argue the episode shows financial interests taking precedence over principles and support for ordinary Russians.

Zelensky: Ukraine Intercepted 60% of Ballistic Missiles in Overnight Russian Attack — Ukraine intercepted 60% of the ballistic missiles launched during Russia’s latest overnight attack, President Volodymyr Zelensky said. The assault included three waves of ballistic strikes on Ukraine and a drone attack on Kyiv, as Zelensky warned that Ukraine is struggling to replenish its air defense missile stocks.

Russian Attack Damages Medical Facility, Homes and School in Odesa — A Russian overnight attack damaged a medical facility, 10 residential buildings and a school in Odesa, with no casualties reported. The strike came amid a sustained campaign targeting the Black Sea port city, while Kyiv was also hit by Russian ballistic missiles and drones.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, September 23, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on September 23, 2026.

Finland, Ukraine Seal Major Drone Deal as Stubb Exposes Russia’s Stalled Donbas Offensive — Finnish President Alexander Stubb told the UN Security Council that Russia’s Donbas push could take years as massive losses barely move the front. Hours later, he and Zelensky signed a Drone Deal expanding joint production, technology transfers, and defense cooperation.

Trump Approval Falls to 33% as Economy Weighs on GOP Ahead of Midterms – CNN Poll — A new CNN poll finds Donald Trump’s approval at its lowest point in CNN polling across his two terms, with economic dissatisfaction emerging as a major issue weeks before the US midterm elections.

Zelensky Urges Strong US Response During Congress Talks as Russian Ballistic Missiles Hit Kyiv — Zelensky said Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv while he was discussing sanctions with US lawmakers in New York. He urged Washington to provide ballistic missile interceptors and implement sanctions against Russia and those helping it earn revenue.

Kyiv Under Attack: Russian Missiles Kill 2, Injure at Least 6 Amid UN Ceasefire Push — Kyiv authorities reported two people killed and at least six injured. Missile debris damaged a maternity hospital, a nearby diagnostic center, and homes across the capital.

‘Tell Your Boss: Enough Is Enough,’ Polish FM Confronts Lavrov at UN — Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski confronted Sergey Lavrov at the UN, rejecting Kremlin claims on Ukraine, invoking Russia’s wartime record, and warning Moscow against further escalation.

Moscow’s Ceasefire Bingo Card – What Might the Kremlin Say to Ukraine’s Unconditional Ceasefire? — “It’s Ukraine’s fault,” “Good idea but…” “What if we try something else?” After Ukraine reiterates its plan for an unconditional ceasefire, here’s a list of potential responses from Moscow based on its past remarks on similar proposals.
